header.title: Pure Culture Sample Schema
header.description: Pure Culture Schema for the AnalysisAPI

sample_name.title: sample name
sample_name.description: The name or label that is present on the shipped sample. This should be a human readable name.

other.title: other
other.description: Other/additional details about your sample that you feel can't be accurately represented in ANY of the available columns.

storage_condt.title: storage condition
storage_condt.description: The storage condition of the sample. This field is NOT multivalued. If selecting other, add the `other_storage_condt` attribute to provide additional detail.

filter_method.title: filter method
filter_method.description: Type of filter used or how the sample was filteres

host_taxid.title: host taxonomy identifier
host_taxid.description: NCBI taxa ID. Format with prefix, NCBITaxon:####

isol_growth_condt.title: isolation and growth condition
isol_growth_condt.description: Publication reference in the form of pubmed ID (pmid), digital object identifier (doi) or url for isolation and growth condition specifications of the organism/material

growth_medium.title: growth medium
growth_medium.description: Method of growth and medium/materials used. Indicate broth, gel, 3-D structure, bioreactor, etc followed by the formula, recipe, or components used to create the growth medium.

other_storage_condt.title: storage condition other
other_storage_condt.description: Please specify your storage conditions if 'other' and the available values are not appropriate

samp_store_temp.title: sample storage temperature
samp_store_temp.description: The temperature at which your samples should be stored upon arrival. This field is NOT multivalued. If selecting other, add the `other_samp_store_temp` attribute to provide additional detail.

analysis_type.title: analysis type
analysis_type.description: The analyses planned for this sample. The analysis types will later be mapped to an allocated resource. This field is constrained to contain only a set of limited terms. Include all the data types. This field can have multiple values separated by a ';'.

technical_reps.title: technical replicates
technical_reps.description: If sending technical replicates of the same sample, indicate the replicate number here.

replicate_number.title: replicate number
replicate_number.description: If samples are biological replicates, indicate the replicate number here.

source_mat_ID.title: source material identifier
source_mat_ID.description: A unique identifier assigned to an original material sample collected or to any derived sub-samples. The source material should be listed as a sample to inform details about parent material relationship.

sample_link.title: sample link
sample_link.description: A unique identifier to assign parent-child, subsample, or sibling samples. This is relevant when a sample or other material was used to generate the new sample. This field allows multiple entries separated by ; (Examples: Soil collected from the field will link with the soil used in an incubation. The soil a plant was grown in links to the plant sample. An original culture sample was transferred to a new vial and generated a new sample)

growth_facil.title: growth facility
growth_facil.description: Type of facility or location from where the sample was collected or grown. This field is NOT multivalued. If selecting other, add the `other_growth_facil` attribute to provide additional detail.

collection_date.title: collection date
collection_date.description: The date of sampling as an instance. Format: YYYY-MM-DD. Also valid, if entire collection date is unknown is just year (YYYY) or just year and month (YYYY-MM)

collection_time.title: collection time
collection_time.description: The time of sampling as an instance (single point). Required format: HH:MM:SS in 24-hour time format. Don't forget the second! (Unit: hh:mm:ss or HH:MM:SS)

sample_collection_dev.title: sample collection device
sample_collection_dev.description: The device used to collect an environmental sample. Include dimensions of device if applicable

other_treatment.title: other treatment
other_treatment.description: Many sample treatment descriptor columns are available. If a treatment is applied to your samples and the provided treatment terms do not satisfy, please add it here. Multiple treatments can be entered here, separated by ;

shipped_sample_size.title: shipped sample size
shipped_sample_size.description: Total amount of sample sent to EMSL. Must include units.

sample_collected.title: sample collected
sample_collected.description: This referes to the TOTAL amount of sample collected from the experiment. NOT the amount sent to EMSL or collected for a specific analysis. Provide value and unit, any unit is valid

sample_collection_method.title: sample collection method
sample_collection_method.description: The method used to collect an environmental sample

sample_processing.title: sample processing
sample_processing.description: A brief description of any processing applied to the sample during or after retrieving the sample from environment, or a link to the relevant protocol(s) performed.

start_date_inc.title: incubation start date
start_date_inc.description: Date the incubation was started. Only relevant for incubation samples. Format: YYYY-MM-DD

watering_regm.title: watering regimen
watering_regm.description: Information about treatment involving an exposure to watering frequencies, treatment regimen including how many times the treatment was repeated, how long each treatment lasted, and the start and end time of the entire treatment; can include multiple regimens

air_temp_regm.title: air temperature regimen
air_temp_regm.description: Information about treatment involving an exposure to varying temperatures; should include the temperature, treatment regimen including how many times the treatment was repeated, how long each treatment lasted, and the start and end time of the entire treatment; can include different temperature regimens

chem_administration.title: chemical administration
chem_administration.description: List of chemical compounds administered to the host or site where sampling occurred, and when (e.g. Antibiotics, n fertilizer, air filter); can include multiple compounds. For chemical entities of biological interest ontology (chebi) (v 163), http://purl.bioontology.org/ontology/chebi

isotope_exposure.title: isotope exposure
isotope_exposure.description: List isotope exposure or addition applied to your sample.

gaseous_environment.title: gaseous environment
gaseous_environment.description: Use of conditions with differing gaseous environments; should include the name of gaseous compound, amount administered, treatment duration, interval and total experimental duration; can include multiple gaseous environment regimens

humidity_regm.title: humidity regimen
humidity_regm.description: Information about treatment involving an exposure to varying degree of humidity; information about treatment involving use of growth hormones; should include amount of humidity administered, treatment regimen including how many times the treatment was repeated, how long each treatment lasted, and the start and end time of the entire treatment; can include multiple regimens

light_regm.title: light regimen
light_regm.description: Information about treatment(s) involving exposure to light, including both light intensity and quality.

biotic_regm.title: biotic regimen
biotic_regm.description: Information about treatment(s) involving use of biotic factors, such as bacteria, viruses or fungi.

extraction_method.title: extraction method
extraction_method.description: If you, the user, performed an extraction, preparation, or processing before sending the sample to EMSL, what was it? This is only applicable when sending an 'analytical sample'. See README for more details on types of samples.

method_development.title: method development
method_development.description: If your samples are TEST sample ONLY, please provide information on what you're hoping this test will resolve.

experimental_factor.title: experimental factor
experimental_factor.description: Experimental factors are essentially the variable aspects of an experiment design which can be used to describe an experiment, or set of experiments, in an increasingly detailed manner. This field accepts ontology terms from Experimental Factor Ontology (EFO) and/or Ontology for Biomedical Investigations (OBI). For a browser of EFO (v 2.95) terms, please see http://purl.bioontology.org/ontology/EFO; for a browser of OBI (v 2018-02-12) terms please see http://purl.bioontology.org/ontology/OBI

experimental_factor_other.title: experimental factor other
experimental_factor_other.description: Other details about your sample that you feel can't be accurately represented in the available columns.

encoded_traits.title: encoded traits
encoded_traits.description: Should include key traits like antibiotic resistance or xenobiotic degradation phenotypes for plasmids, converting genes for phage

propagation.title: propagation
propagation.description: This field is specific to different taxa. For phages: lytic/lysogenic, for plasmids: incompatibility group, for eukaryotes: sexual/asexual.

ref_biomaterial.title: reference for biomaterial
ref_biomaterial.description: Primary publication if isolated before genome publication; otherwise, primary genome report.

host_spec_range.title: host specificity or range
host_spec_range.description: The range and diversity of host species that an organism is capable of infecting, defined by NCBI taxonomy identifier. Format with prefix, NCBITaxon:####

subspecf_gen_lin.title: subspecific genetuc lineage
subspecf_gen_lin.description: Information about the genetic distinctness of the sequenced organism below the subspecies level, e.g., serovar, serotype, biotype, ecotype, or any relevant genetic typing schemes like Group I plasmid. Supply both the lineage name and the lineage rank separated by a colon, e.g., biovar:abc123

trophic_level.title: trophic level
trophic_level.description: Trophic levels are the feeding position in a food chain. Microbes can be a range of producers.

pathogenicity.title: pathogenicity
pathogenicity.description: To what is the entity pathogenic

samp_biotic_relationship.title: sample biotic relationship
samp_biotic_relationship.description: Description of relationship(s) between the subject organism and other organism(s) it is associated with. E.g., parasite on species X; mutualist with species Y. The target organism is the subject of the relationship, and the other organism(s) is the object

non_microb_biomass_method.title: non microbial biomass method
non_microb_biomass_method.description: Reference or method used in determining biomass

non_microb_biomass.title: non microbial biomass
non_microb_biomass.description: Amount of biomass; should include the name for the part of biomass measured, e.g.insect, plant, total (Unit: µm)

genetic_mod.title: genetic modification
genetic_mod.description: Genetic modifications of the genome of an organism, which may occur naturally by spontaneous mutation, or be introduced by some experimental means, e.g. specification of a transgene or the gene knocked-out or details of transient transfection
